boundary: Scope: Spec 010 OSF deposit action (pilot DESIGN §4); the osf_metadata mapping in tekmerion.deposit is the contract and is not modified by this spec

evidence.ref: specs/010-osf-registration/spec.md (design decision: the mapping is the contract)

falsification_tests: F-010-1: an OSF record produced by the deposit action whose title, description, tags, component set, file set, or registration summary differs from osf_metadata(that bundle's manifest), or a deposit API parameter that lets a caller override any of them.
claims.text: Every OSF-visible field of a deposit — project title, description, category, tags, the component set, each component's file set, and the registration's summary — is computed from osf_metadata of the deposited bundle's manifest. No code path accepts a caller-supplied title, description, or component structure for the record.

boundary: Scope: Spec 010 OSF deposit action; the approval gate is DESIGN §4.2.1's identical application of the WS5 §3 gate in tekmerion.deposit.deposit_bundle
falsification_tests: F-010-2: a refusal case (empty approver, tampered bundle, unfrozen bundle) in which any OSF object was created before the refusal, observed via a counting transport in tests.
claims.text: The deposit refuses, before creating any OSF object, when approved_by is empty, when the bundle does not verify standalone, or when the bundle's manifest carries no freeze binding (missing registration_hash or checkpoint_root).

boundary: Scope: repeat attempts that have the deposit state or the project GUID available to the check; a from-nothing run cannot know a prior project exists (recorded in plan.md, not hidden)
falsification_tests: F-010-3: two distinct registration GUIDs binding the same study + schema after a repeat deposit attempt that had the deposit state or the project GUID available.
claims.text: Submission is idempotent: before creating a draft registration the action checks for an existing registration binding the same registration_hash under the same schema (deposit state first; the project's registration list when a project GUID is known), and a repeat attempt creates no second registration — it reports the existing registration's GUID and URL.

boundary: Scope: Spec 010 OSF transport + deposit action; a 429 is a stop, never a retry (the Zenodo transport's rule, adopted unchanged)

evidence.ref: specs/010-osf-registration/spec.md (design decisions: transport shape; deposit state + idempotency)

falsification_tests: F-010-4: a swallowed provider error, an automatically retried create that produced a duplicate OSF object, or a resumed run that re-created the project or components instead of continuing from the recorded state.
claims.text: Provider failures abort the action with the provider's actual HTTP status and response body carried in the error; an ambiguous create is never retried blind into a duplicate; partial progress is persisted to the deposit state and a later run resumes from it instead of starting over.

boundary: Scope: Spec 010 receipt + verify_osf_anchor; comparison is against the deposited bundle's osf_metadata anchor_values (plan.md ambiguity 5)
falsification_tests: F-010-5: verify_osf_anchor passing on a fetched record whose stated checkpoint root, bundle hash, or registration hash differs from the bundle's anchor values, or whose component structure diverges from the mapping.
claims.text: A completed deposit returns a receipt (mechanism, root, bundle hash, registration hash, project GUID, registration GUID, URL/DOI, approver, anchored-at, embargo state), and verify_osf_anchor independently re-fetches the registration from the OSF API and passes only if the fetched record states the mapping's anchor values and the project structure matches the component mapping.

boundary: Scope: the T-P4 demonstration only; the anchor.recorded ledgering of DESIGN §4.2.4 remains the flow for future live studies and is test-exercised on fixtures (plan.md ambiguity 1)
falsification_tests: F-010-6: any differing file hash in specs/002-mvp-implementation/evaluation/study/ across the demonstration, or a receipt written anywhere inside that directory.
claims.text: The T-P4 demonstration modifies nothing in the Phase 7 study directory: every file's bytes are identical before and after (hashes recorded), and the registration references the study externally — the receipt lives in this spec's records, not in the frozen study's ledger or bundles.

boundary: Scope: DESIGN §4.2.3's embargo demonstration requirement; the demonstration registration itself is public/immediate (plan.md ambiguity 2)
falsification_tests: F-010-7: embargo support claimed in any record without a fetched-back test registration record showing embargoed = true and the embargo end date as set.
claims.text: The embargo path is demonstrated, not asserted: a test registration created with an embargo end date is fetched back showing the embargoed state (not public, the embargo end date as set) before embargo support is claimed anywhere.

boundary: Scope: all Spec 010 surfaces and any pilot material describing OSF anchoring (DESIGN §6 evidence pack language included)
falsification_tests: F-010-8: any presentation of an OSF registration as validating a study's verdicts or as human acceptance, or a verification path that reads anchor values from the mutable project instead of the registration record.
claims.text: SCOPE: an OSF registration is an anchor and a discovery record, not a validation: it certifies that this bundle, stating these anchor values, was snapshotted at a point in time. It does not certify the study's verdicts, is not lane-2 acceptance of anything, and — because the OSF project remains editable after registration — anchor verification reads the values from the registration record, never from the live project.
